description:
PROBLEM: tests/unit/test_canary_impact_live.py costs about 388 s of PR CI (ranks 2-7). Two class-level fixtures (lines ~29-45) each run a whole-tree `pytest --collect-only` subprocess plus a dependency-map build (about 80-100 s each, local), rebuilt on every worker. The bodies take about 10 s. Worse, the four test_known_regressions_are_selected replays all hit the whole-suite fallback (unmapped_path) and select every test, so `expected <= selected` cannot fail; test_monitoring_lazy_export_selects_resource_monitoring passes through a dynamic-file edge the same way.

CHANGES:
1. Add an optional paths parameter to collect_canary_node_ids (scripts/canary_impact.py or wherever it lives) so a caller can collect only named test files; default behaviour unchanged.
2. Rewrite test_known_regressions_are_selected: one module-level fixture builds the dependency map and collection for only the target files; each case passes only the changed paths that have a mapped edge and asserts whole_suite is False, the target file is selected, and its selection reasons include a `dependency` edge (dynamic reasons may coexist). Keep one assertion that replays the real full diff and checks `expected <= selected`, so the test still notices if the fallback rules change.
3. Rewrite the monitoring test the same way: assert a dependency edge from benchbox performance.py to test_resource_monitoring.py.
4. Move test_every_collected_file_has_a_per_file_edge and test_medium_single_module_diff_selects_subset to a new module marked slow, with module-level fixtures (removes the class-scoped fixture deprecation warning), subject to decision gate G2.

DECISION GATES:
G1 Before rewriting, read tracker items canary-impact-03-replay-and-go-decision and canary-impact-04-shadow-job; if either relies on these tests' current semantics, record how the rewrite preserves or strengthens that and proceed; do not change scripts/canary_impact.py selection behaviour.
G2 Moving to slow is allowed only if (a) a scheduled workflow runs the slow tier on develop including the new module (show nightly.yml or release-canary selection and a run that executes slow tests), and (b) the coverage map / selection evidence shows PRs editing scripts/canary_impact.py would not have selected these two tests anyway OR the PR body accepts per-push to nightly with that evidence. If (a) fails, keep them in medium in a separate module with one module-level fixture and record the decision.
G3 Mutation (C2): with the rewritten tests, break the dependency edge for each regression target (for example drop the import-graph edge in the selector input or rename the imported symbol in a temp copy) and show the matching case fails; show the old test passed under the same break (it could not fail).
G4 Exactness: verify the per-file dependency map equals the full-tree map's entries for all three target files, not only one.
